transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well, what finally made me come in and say something is that... after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. And then I just come back down and act as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed. It's become a problem, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes, I do. When no one is in the kitchen, I can go through a lot of food. I'll eat leftovers from a church supper, crackers, cheese, cookies... whatever I baked for my book club. I just eat it all in one sitting. It is far more than I would ever serve myself at a normal meal.
When you have these episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you’re eating?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start... it just feels like a switch flips. It's like I'm watching myself keep eating, and part of me is in there saying, 'Linda, stop now,' but I just can't do it. My hands just keep reaching for more food, no matter what I tell myself.
How often do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen?

Well, since last winter, it's been happening pretty regularly. There has hardly been a week when I haven’t had at least one of those private eating spells. And then I always try to make up for it... either by throwing up, skipping my meals the next day, or just really overdoing it with my walking.
How much does your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself?

It affects me a lot, honestly. Um, my daughter and a friend from church have actually told me I look too thin lately. But... I just don't see it. If my skirt feels even a little snug, or if the scale goes up just a single pound, I panic. It feels like I've somehow become huge overnight, and I just can't stand the thought of gaining weight.
Have you become significantly underweight for your height?

No, I don't think so. I mean, even though my daughter said I look thin, my actual weight on the scale is... well, it's pretty average for my height. I haven't dropped to a weight where someone would say I'm dangerously thin or anything like that. I just really don't want it to go up.
During those eating episodes, do you eat much more rapidly than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed myself eating any faster than normal during those times. I mean... I'm definitely eating a lot more food than I should, but I'm not really rushing through it or anything like that. I just sort of keep going.
During those eating episodes, do you usually keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

No, not really. I mean, I eat a lot, but I don't think I push it to the point where I'm physically uncomfortable or in pain from being too full. I just eat more than I planned to, but I don't get that stuffed, uncomfortable feeling.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or upset?

No, I wouldn't say they cause me a lot of distress. I mean... I know I'm eating more than I intend to, but I don't really get upset about it. It's just something that happens, and then I just kind of move on with my day. I'm not agonizing over it, if that's what you mean.
Outside of the binge episodes, do you usually restrict how much you eat in order to lose weight?
No, I don't really do that either. I eat pretty normally the rest of the time. I'm not trying to diet or cut back on what I eat to lose weight. I just eat regular meals.
On average, do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen at least twice a week?

Well, I'd say since last winter, it's been pretty consistent. There's hardly been a week where I haven't had at least one of those times where I eat a lot in private and then try to undo it. Whether it's throwing up, or skipping meals the next day, or just doing way too much walking to burn it off... it happens at least once a week, maybe twice sometimes, but definitely regularly.
For the past 3 months, have these binge-and-vomit episodes happened at least once a week?

Yes, definitely. Like I was just saying, since last winter, it's been very consistent. There's hardly been a single week where I haven't had at least one of those private eating spells and then tried to make up for it somehow—whether that's throwing up, skipping my meals the next day, or just pushing myself way too hard walking. So yes, definitely at least once a week for the past three months.

latest_inference.note: Weekly binge eating with loss of control for >3 months, recurrent compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise), and overvaluation of weight/shape are sufficient for bulimia nervosa. Normal weight argues against anorexia nervosa binge-purge type; lack of marked distress and BED-associated features rules out binge eating disorder/other specified eating disorder.
